sections.heading: Bottom-up estimates
sections.detail: committed first — timestamp above, before any market number
sections.markdown:
**Sources (primary, this session, no sell-side data):** AMD Q2 2026 8-K (2026-08-04, accession 0000002488-26-000121) — segments, P&L, Q3 guide, balance sheet; AMD Q4/FY2025 release (2026-02-03) + FY2025 10-K — FY23-25 comparatives, cash flows, assets; AMD Q2 2026 call (2026-08-04) — 2027 DC-doubling guide, Helios ramp, customers; "Advancing AI 2026" (2026-07-23) — MI450 spec, ROCm.ai claims, TAM; hyperscaler Q2 2026 capex reports.

**EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS gate (run first):**
- Accruals (NI−CFO)/avg total assets: FY23 ≈ **−1.2%**; FY24 ≈ **−2.0%**; FY25 ≈ **−4.7%** — persistently negative, CFO exceeds NI every year (~1.8-1.95x), strong cash conversion.
- Divergence flags: none manipulation-class. MI308 inventory (~$360m prior charges reversed in Q4'25, 8-K) optics-class, disclosed, not a haircut trigger.
- Structure: US large-cap 10-K filer, no VIE, no going-concern language; AMD's up-to-$5bn Anthropic investment (customer) disclosed, arms-length — not a governance flag.
- Action rule: no confirmed manipulation-class flag → gate clears, proceed.

**Revenue build (segment, USD):** Q2'26 actuals: Data Center $6,718m (+107% YoY, 58% of revenue; op income $2,103m, 31.3% margin), Client $3,062m (+23%), Gaming $779m (−31%), Embedded $977m (+19%, op income $386m, 40% margin); total $11,536m (+50%). Q3'26 guided ~$13.0B (±$300m) at ~56% non-GAAP GM. Forward build uses the call's H2 DC acceleration guide:
- FY2026E: DC ~$30.3B (+~94%) / Client ~$12.4B / Gaming ~$3.4B / Embedded ~$4.0B → **~$50.1B (+45%)**
- FY2027E: DC ~$62B (**"more than double," +~105% — the load-bearing guide**) / Client ~$13.5B / Gaming ~$2.9B / Embedded ~$4.6B → **~$83.0B (+66%)**
- FY2028E: DC ~$85B (+~37%, decelerating) / non-DC ~$22.6B → **~$107.6B (+30%)**

**Margin path (non-GAAP):** GM held flat at 56% (Q2'26 print; Q3'26 guide) — no expansion assumed. Segment op margins scale as in Q2'26: DC 31.3% → ~33%; Embedded 40%; Client+Gaming 15%. Non-GAAP op income: FY26E ~$13.7B → FY27E ~$24.8B → FY28E ~$32.8B.

**Owner-earnings bridge (§5; SBC subtracted):** tax ~13% (guided); net interest +~$0.4B (net cash ~$10B); SBC $1.64B (FY25) +15%/yr. Owner earnings (non-GAAP NI − SBC): FY26E ~$10.4B (**~$6.3/sh**) → FY27E ~$19.8B (**~$11.9/sh**) → FY28E ~$26.4B (**~$15.9/sh**) on ~1,660m shares. FCF: Q2'26 capex $808m (vs ~$298m run-rate) for Helios capacity; FY26E capex ~$2.5-3.0B → FCF ~$9-10B, ~$20B by FY27E. ROIIC not cleanly computable on R&D-heavy semis; the revealed preference is DC op income swinging −$155m → +$2,103m YoY.

**3-assumption sensitivity (inputs carrying >70% of value):**
1. **FY2027E DC revenue** (dominant, ~70% of FY27E EPS): base $62B ("more than double," call); bull ~$70B; bear ~$45B (2027 capex trim or MI450 slip).
2. **DC operating margin**: base 32-33%; bull 35%; bear 27% (rack BOM dilution, pricing).
3. **MI450 competitive execution**: base = credible #2 on the 432GB HBM4 inference-TCO edge; bear = independent benchmarks show parity-or-worse and the ~80-85% NVIDIA share ceiling holds.

sections.heading: Priors disclosure
sections.detail: one sentence, from memory, written before document work
sections.markdown: What I believe the market narrative is: AMD is NVIDIA's distant #2 — a share-loser in AI GPUs whose elevated multiple rests on the EPYC hyperscaler buildout, and which "disappointed" on Q3 guidance despite a record quarter.

sections.heading: Variant perception
sections.markdown:
**Market believes:** AMD is a losing NVIDIA-beta. The Q2'26 print (record revenue, DC +107%) still fell ~9% after hours because the Q3 guide "only" beat the published midpoint expectation, not the whisper — proof the multiple is stretched. MI400 is architecturally behind Blackwell/Rubin; ROCm will never match CUDA; ~80-85% NVIDIA accelerator share caps AMD.

**Why wrong:** Three primary-source facts the market mis-prices. (1) **The dated 2027 guide**: Su (Q2'26 call) guided DC revenue to "more than double" in 2027, growth "well above 100%," calling a ~$30B 2027 Instinct estimate "probably too low" — the market read the Q3 guide as a miss, ignoring that 2027, not Q3, is the story. (2) **MI450 is competitive on inference TCO**: 432GB HBM4 (vs Rubin R200's 288GB) fits a 405B-parameter FP8 model on one GPU; AMD claims Helios delivers up to +30% tokens/dollar vs Rubin NVL72. (3) **The TAM is expanding, not fixed**: hyperscaler capex ~$725B in 2026 (+77% YoY), ~$1T 2027E; OpenAI 6GW + Meta 6GW + Anthropic 2GW MI450 commitments scale AMD ~2x WITHOUT stealing NVIDIA share. The non-AI base (Client +23%, Embedded +19% at 40% op margin) is self-funding through the ramp.

**What proves us wrong:** MI450 independent benchmarks at TCO parity-or-worse; any named hyperscaler cuts 2027 capex; DC op margin compresses below ~27%; or Helios/MI450 revenue in the Q4'26 print lags the embedded ramp.

**Edge taxonomy:** **(a) analytical** — the market mis-models AMD as share-loss in a fixed pie; it is a TAM-expansion #2 with a memory-capacity TCO position. Secondary **(b) informational-synthesis** — connecting the 2027 doubling guide to hyperscaler capex and the MI450 HBM4 spec. Not (c)/(d). Honest caveat: this is a momentum continuation, not a value buy — at the current print the market already embeds FY2027E execution at ~36-40x owner earnings, and my disciplined DCF (9-10% COE, SBC-subtracted) puts fair EV roughly 0-20% below spot. The edge is the dated 2027 catalyst plus the reversal filter, not cheapness; EV is thin (+2.7%), size small.

sections.heading: Disconfirming facts
sections.detail: >=3, observable, current, each citing a filing/IR line
sections.markdown:
1. NVIDIA holds ~80-85% of AI accelerators and ~85-90% of training workloads; AMD's +30% tokens/dollar claim is AMD's own, unvalidated by independent benchmarks (Advancing AI 2026) — a parity print caps #2 intake at the current share ceiling.
2. The 2027 doubling is guidance, not contracted revenue; the named 14GW buildout depends on hyperscaler capex staying elevated — GOOGL posted negative FCF in Q2'26 and MSFT is power-constrained (hyperscaler Q2'26 reports); one capex trim cuts the load-bearing assumption.
3. ROCm remains structurally behind CUDA (no TensorRT-LLM equivalent); AMD's ROCm.ai "3.3x" claim is vs its own prior stack, not vs CUDA.
4. The non-AI base is itself softening: Gaming −31% YoY, Client+Gaming op margin down to 15% (from 21%) (Q2'26 PR) — it can cushion, not rescue, a DC stumble.
5. The Q2'26 tape is the valuation trap in miniature: record revenue + EPS beat still sold off ~9% — at an elevated multiple, even good prints disappoint; +183.7%/12m at ~79% vol carries acute "good news not good enough" reversal risk.
6. HBM4 spot prices reportedly surged ~435% (Bear's wccftech cite, not independently validated) — MI450's 432GB HBM4 "memory edge" is ~1.5x exposure to a scarce, price-spiking input that pressures the 31.3%→33% DC margin path and the +30% tokens/$ TCO claim (Advancing AI 2026).

sections.heading: Pre-mortem
sections.markdown: It is mid-2027 and this position lost ~22%+. The most likely reason is a sharp momentum reversal, not a fundamentals blow-up: the run carried +183.7%/12m at ~79% vol, and a "good news not good enough" print or a hyperscaler trimming 2027 capex triggered a violent de-rating as the market stopped rolling forward EPS, compressing the ~40x owner-earnings multiple toward the ~25-30x my DCF says is fair. The 2027 doubling was management's word, not contracted revenue, and the first slippage sign — Helios revenue in the Q4'26 print below the ramp — cracked the narrative faster than the business deteriorated.
